Question
========
Take a look at the following XML snippet:

```
<Bike number=190416>
  <state>ok</state>
</bike>
```

What is wrong with it?

Answerlist
----------
* Nothing - this is valid, well-formed XML.
* The attribute value `190416` is not enclosed in quotes, and the start tag `<Bike>` does not match its end tag `</bike>`, since element names are case sensitive.
* The element `<state>` is not allowed to contain text content.
* The attribute name `number` is a reserved keyword and cannot be used in XML.


Solution
========
Two separate mistakes make this snippet invalid. First, attribute values always need to be quoted, so `number=190416` should be written as `number="190416"`. Second, since element names are case sensitive, `<Bike>` and `</bike>` are treated as different element names entirely, so the start and end tag never actually match - it should either open with `<Bike>` and close with `</Bike>`, or use lower case consistently throughout.

----------
* False
* True

* False
